lanes.name: unit
lanes.description: pytest over tests/unit and tests/contract. Mostly in-process: contract tests use FastAPI TestClient (httpx, already a transitive dep) against the real router tree, so they need no port. Not strictly in-process, and the description used to claim otherwise: a few cases deliberately spawn bounded child interpreters (test_egress_backstop_unit.py's C14 probes, test_egress_backstop_subprocess.py's C11/C12, test_soak_run.py), each with an explicit subprocess timeout so a hung child fails the gate instead of hanging it. That is allowed here; an unbounded subprocess is not. Since 2026-10-04 (025, review M3) it deselects the marker verify_control_live: those cases spawn real child processes and have their own lane, verify-control.
lanes.command: uv run pytest tests/unit tests/contract -m "not verify_control_live" --cov=src/reader3_app --cov-report=json:coverage-unit.json --cov-report=term
lanes.probeCommand: uv run pytest tests/unit tests/contract -m "not verify_control_live" --collect-only -q

lanes.name: verify-control
lanes.description: The tests/unit/test_verify_control_* cases marked verify_control_live: every one spawns a child process (control.py as a subprocess, fake reader3/reader3-server/browse executables, ps/lsof, node, and in C66 the real reader3 and reader3-server). Split out of the unit lane on 2026-10-04 (025, review M3): with them in, the unit lane ran ~9 min idle and 28-33 min under load against its 600 s timeout, and its description (in-process, a few bounded children) no longer matched what it ran. Measured 2026-10-04: 389 passed in 725 s wall at load average 14-40; timeoutMs 2400000 is ~3.3x that. Same commit gate as unit, by user decision; only the timeout and the honesty of the description differ. The marker is assigned mechanically: a case that starts any subprocess.Popen in setup, call or teardown carries it, a case that starts none stays in the unit lane. Wall-clock asserts in these cases (elapsed_s < 6, < 8) can fail on a heavily loaded machine; that is an environment failure, rerun before reading it as a regression. No --cov: the code lives under .claude/skills/, outside --cov=src/reader3_app, and most cases reach it only through a subprocess (review M2).
lanes.command: uv run pytest tests/unit tests/contract -m verify_control_live
lanes.probeCommand: uv run pytest tests/unit tests/contract -m verify_control_live --collect-only -q

lanes.name: e2e
lanes.description: Playwright via pytest-playwright against a live reader3-server started by the live_server fixture in tests/e2e/conftest.py (free port, --port, READER3_BOOKS_DIR -> tmp, polls /api/health). gateOn was EMPTY until 2026-08-26: an empty tests/e2e/ makes the lane report 'never passed' forever, which denies every push and trains everyone into permanent TDD_GUARD_BYPASS=1. The 009 harness spike added the first test and restored gateOn to ["push"] in the same commit, as required. Do not set READER3_TOKEN for this lane: the frontend fetch does not carry the token yet, so the token gate would 401 every write. Since 021 (2026-10-01) the command runs through scripts/e2e_lock.py, an fcntl lock on ~/.cache/reader3-e2e.flock that the kernel releases when the run ends; a held lock exits 75 (BUSY <owner>), which is an environment failure, not a test result. Check it with `uv run python scripts/e2e_lock.py status`.
lanes.command: uv run python scripts/e2e_lock.py -- uv run pytest tests/e2e --browser chromium

lanes.name: packaging
lanes.description: Builds a wheel, installs it into a clean venv with dependencies resolved at LATEST (uv.lock deliberately not used), starts a real reader3-server and hits four routes. The only place in the repo that would notice a dependency major bump breaking the installed app -- uv run and the unit lane both go through the pinned lock and stay green. ~50s measured 2026-09-03 (an earlier note said ~17s; that predates the current dependency set and the latest-version resolution it does on every run). Still gates on push, not on commit -- and the gap is the reason: at 17s someone would argue for moving it to commit, at 50s nobody will. This lane carried C11/C12 of WI-3 from 2026-09-07 until later the same day; they moved to tests/unit/test_egress_backstop_subprocess.py and the unit lane. Two reasons, in order: they are test-harness correctness and have nothing to do with wheels, so a 'do not prune these' comment was the only thing holding them here; and the cost argument was measured wrong (~1.9s against a ~44s unit lane, not ~3s against a ~4s one). This lane is wheel smoke only -- if a case here does not concern the installed artifact, it is in the wrong lane.
